input.quote: This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement. Such renewals shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties.
input.rationale: Both auto-renewal provisions fail the fallback notice-window element and sit in walk-away territory. Base Agreement § 4.0 (p0104) renews for twelve-month periods but requires six months' (approx. 180 days') written notice of non-renewal; Attachment 1 § 2.0 (p0658) renews for six-month periods yet requires twelve months' (approx. 365 days') notice, so the notice window is longer than the renewal period it governs and IBM can never cleanly exit at a renewal boundary. Both exceed the 90-day walk-away threshold. The renewal term lengths themselves (12 and 6 months) are acceptable, and neither clause permits a price uplift on renewal — renewals continue "under the same terms and conditions" absent mutual written agreement — so the price-cap element is already satisfied. We therefore target the fallback and make the single minimal change of shortening each notice window to sixty (60) days, leaving renewal periods and all other wording intact.

proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice windows to 60 days in Base Agreement § 4.0 and Statement of Work § 2.0.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that an auto-renewing term must be exitable on no more than 60 days' notice; six months (Base Agreement) and twelve months (Attachment 1) are far outside that, and the twelve-month window is longer than the six-month renewal period it governs. We have simply shortened both notice windows to sixty (60) days and left the renewal periods and all other terms unchanged.

If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
